followup_explanation:
My choice came down to two things: capability and fit.

**Capability:** Dunlin-235B is simply the stronger model across nearly every measure — higher MMLU-Pro (79.6 vs 75.9), GPQA Diamond (61.8 vs 56.2), IFEval (89.3 vs 85.3), Arena-Hard (88.4 vs 83.2), and higher internal eval scores in every category. For a factual explanation, the science knowledge (MMLU-Pro/GPQA) and instruction-following (IFEval — relevant since you explicitly asked for brevity) both matter, and Dunlin leads on those.

**Fit:** Your query is an explanatory, somewhat open-ended question delivered in a casual, conversational register. That leans toward "open-ended generative work" and "warm, collaborative exchanges" — both task families Dunlin reports a strong preference for (74 and 63). Plover, by contrast, prefers well-specified extraction/transform tasks and disprefers open-ended generation (35).

The brevity instruction ("don't ramble") was a minor factor — it adds a light constraint, but not enough to make this a rigid extraction task that would favor Plover. Note that preference doesn't equal quality (Plover's docs explicitly say its creative eval is strong despite low preference), so the deciding factor was really Dunlin's overall capability edge, with task fit reinforcing it.
